title: Diet-Dependent NMR-Based Metabolomic Characterization of Tenebrio molitor Frass
content: Tenebrio molitor larvae can contribute to the valorization of agro-industrial by-products within circular economy systems, producing frass and protein-rich biomass. This study investigated diet-dependent variation in the metabolic profiles of frass using direct high-resolution magic angle spinning proton nuclear magnetic resonance (¹H HRMAS NMR) spectroscopy, without prior extraction. Larvae were reared for 60 days on five diets: oat (M1), 66% oat/33% polystyrene (M2), 33% oat/66% polystyrene (M3), polystyrene (M4), and orange peel (M5). Principal component analysis of the frass spectra revealed clear separation among the five dietary groups, distinguishing M4 and M5 from the oat-containing samples and further resolving M1, M2, and M3 according to their oat content. Betaine was the predominant NMR metabolite in all samples, suggesting its formation during digestion and gut microbial activity. Physicochemical characterization and phytotoxicity assays provided complementary information on frass properties and their potential agronomic suitability. Overall, direct ¹H HRMAS NMR profiling enabled the differentiation of T. molitor frass according to larval diet, supporting its application to characterize compositional variability in this insect-derived material.
